answers.assumption_check: Two load-bearing assumptions, both measured or bounded. (a) The inner seal overrides CAIRN_TESTER_REACH_LOG for its own children (device.py run_env sets it per run), so an outer logger reached by the chain only duplicates lines into the inner log; skipping it loses nothing the outer seal reads. Read at cairn/devices/tester/device.py:782-785 on 2026-11-21. (b) A reach logger can be told from a non-reach sitecustomize by a marker constant the module itself carries, not by its directory name, so a worktree or scratch copy is still recognised. The build must add that marker; the old logger (pre-build bytes) carries none, which is why clause 2 seeds the second reach dir from the built bytes.
answers.builder_check: A Haiku builder needs: (1) where the chain-load is: the end of cairn/devices/tester/reach/sitecustomize.py, the loop that finds the next sitecustomize on sys.path past _HERE; (2) the marker: a module-level constant, e.g. CAIRN_TESTER_REACH_LOGGER = True, read from the candidate file's text (a plain substring check, no import) before exec; (3) the module must still import nothing from cairn; (4) the proof uses cairn.tools.scratch.scratch.scratch_dir for every temp dir (bare tempfile in tester proofs is red under f92d213f7dd0's proof), runs children with sys.executable and an env with PYTHONPATH and CAIRN_TESTER_REACH_LOG set explicitly, and parses the log as JSON lines {pid, files}; (5) PROVES = {'0bfd1a530cd4': {'1': ..., '4': ...}}. All five are written into the ticket's how and falsifier.

answers.collision_check: 734b22d09f2e (a seal records the components its run reached) chose to chain-load the next sitecustomize so a shadowed system hook still runs; its WHY is that the shadowed hook's behaviour must not differ under a seal. This ticket keeps that why (clause 4 is 734b's clause 4) and narrows only which sitecustomize counts as 'next': never another reach logger. A distinction, not a collision. 0a807f816e9f repaired its own proof (tooth 4) and stays PROVED; this ticket removes the cause, after which tooth 4 is still correct.
answers.falsifier_check: Four clauses at cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_reach_logger_chains_past_another_reach_logger.py, run under bin/cairn test: (1) [this tree's reach, a second reach dir whose logger writes a marker] loads only this tree's logger: marker absent, one log line per pid; (2) the reverse order loads only the second's; (3) neither order prints 'Error in sitecustomize' or RecursionError; (4) a real non-reach sitecustomize further down still runs. Horizon: red at HEAD (the chain loads the second reach logger and recurses), green with the build.
